title: Man Pleads Not Guilty in 2024 Threats Against Laredo Elementary Schools
excerpt: Juan Carlos Moreno, 41, pleaded not guilty Oct. 8 in 406th District Court to a terroristic-threat charge stemming from a note left at a Laredo behavioral health center in October 2024 that put local schools on secure mode, according to the Laredo Morning Times.
content:
Juan Carlos Moreno, 41, pleaded not guilty on Oct. 8, 2026, in the 406th District Court before Judge David E. Garcia to a terroristic-threat charge stemming from a note left at a Laredo behavioral health center in October 2024, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Moreno is charged with terroristic threat of a public servant involving public fear, serious bodily injury or influence of government, a third-degree felony carrying 2 to 10 years in prison, the newspaper reported. He remains in custody and is represented by court-appointed attorney Ted Kim. His defense also requested a bond reduction related to new charges for which bonds had been set at the magistrate level.

The underlying incident happened on Oct. 22, 2024, when a note was left taped to the door of the Border Region Behavioral Health Center, 1500 Pappas St., according to the newspaper. Staff reported it at about 7:42 a.m. that Tuesday. The note included general threats against elementary schools and detailed references to school shootings. Laredo police recommended a lockdown, and schools were placed on secure mode. Investigators notified Laredo ISD, United ISD and other private and charter schools, and United ISD spokeswoman Officer Sylvia Abrego said all United ISD campuses were placed on secure mode.

Moreno was arrested in October 2024 in the 500 block of Montgomery Street, located based on his prior record, the newspaper reported. No weapons were found on him or on his property. He was arrested by the Laredo Police Department Violent Crime Gang Unit.

Police Chief Miguel A. Rodriguez Jr. described Moreno as having a history of violent encounters with police, a mental-health history, and as a public threat, according to the newspaper. Police said his criminal history included aggravated assault against a public servant, aggravated assault, assault, drug possession, deadly conduct and robbery charges, among others.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 14, 2026.
